items.title: Bill Dobbins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: And sometime, this must have been in the early 80s or so, not long before Gil passed, Gil Evans died — it was funny he had that kind of wild electric band, but he was on the show.

ctx.x: Baroque composers were writing music and the music was contrapuntal, there was no system of harmony. People weren’t thinking about chord progressions in Bach’s time. All the Baroque music was composed and improvised in relation to melodic figures. And the composers and improvisers, first of all, everybody improvised then, because it was a part of the musical process, the musical common practice. And when Bach was writing inventions and fugues and things he wasn’t hearing a chord progression, he was starting with…

saying I’m going to substitute chords for everything, almost invariably the essence of what the original bass line, or what the original progression was, is there. It’s just that maybe instead of a six chord or a six nine chord for the tonic, they’ll use a dominant seventh chord of some kind. Instead of a two minor chord, a two five, the two will be some kind of dominant seventh, a secondary dominant, or a half diminished, which is a little more colorful. And then they also find ways of using passing tones and…
